correctness.rationale: For the repaired signed geometry, row cancellation gives y=−x+sum(V)−sum(U) on a fixed edge. At n≥6 the derangement matches disjoint pairs and bounds |x+y| by 2(n−4); four feasible corners have values in an interval of length one. This also corrects the frozen proof's informal 'full sum of absolute coefficients' wording: sign potentials of magnitude 1/2 take half that sum, exactly the claimed norm. At n=5 symmetrization preserves the pair, and distances imply |z|≤2, |z−x|≤2 for z=q−p, hence |y|+|x|≤4. The three prescribed tests and negatives satisfy the metric conditions on all six support points and extend by the explicit McShane formula. Convex combinations fill the respective regions and their support functions give all signs and zero coefficients. The common-neighbor identity is valid on diagonal, disjoint and intersecting entries and J vanishes on the quotient. An independently constructed edge-potential LP anchoring one vertex agreed exactly numerically on all 49 integer coefficient pairs −3…3 for each of n=5,6; replay with graph disjointness, two inequalities per edge, and fixed edge objective. Independent heat LP checks at t=0,0.001,0.05,0.3,1.4 matched the original formula to 6e−16; its increasing log-rate and t=0 Petersen degeneracy also follow by differentiating the exact two-exponential formula. Those finite checks are not an all-n proof. The frozen verification and both checkers were inspected, not executed.

evidence: Bourne et al.: for a regular graph the p-idleness function is linear on [1/(k+1),1], with slope equal to minus the condensed curvature.

Bonini et al.: k times condensed curvature is c+2−(m−M), where c is the common-neighbor count, m the size of each exclusive neighbor set and M their maximum bipartite matching size. It is zero for Petersen and c+2 for the derangement matching in n≥6.
Münch–Wojciechowski relates curvature lower bounds and heat gradient bounds.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The first two results together are stronger coverage of the high-idleness heat mechanism, beyond a mere exponential bound. Their normalized measures require nonnegative probabilities and do not address the mixed-sign sector or establish the whole pair region.

evidence: For β≥0 and α≥β with s=α+kβ>0, set p=α/s≥1/(k+1). Kantorovich duality and high-idleness linearity give the norm s(1−(1−p)κ)=α+(k−kκ)β. Substituting α_t=((n−3)a+b)/(n−2) and β_t=(a−b)/(n−2), a=e^{−(k−1)t}, b=e^{−(k+n−3)t}, gives exactly both frozen heat formulas. The omitted monotonicity and Petersen Taylor term are direct derivatives of those formulas.

The centrally symmetric hull of (0,±4),(1,3),(−1,−3) has identical support in every nonnegative direction but lacks (1,−3),(−1,3); for (α,β)=(−4,1) the hull gives 4 whereas the proved Petersen region gives 7.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The original heat result is mechanically implied even if its specialized formula is not printed elsewhere. The repaired joint region requires signed support information not determined by any restriction to nonnegative walk coefficients. Its Petersen opposite-sign extremes follow from the added exact test potentials rather than the curvature formula.

originality.rationale: The remaining exact joint feasible regions support arbitrary real signed filters. Positive-walk idleness results cover the removed heat finding and the positive support directions, not the claimed full geometry. The opposite-sign Petersen corners in particular require additional feasible potentials; no matching signed-region statement was found in the inspected sources. The all-signed shape is retained as one invariant, not each sign sector as a separate novelty claim.
residual_risks: The search does not establish historical priority for the joint signed region under another polytope or signed-transport description. Known high-idleness, heat, spectral and matching consequences are not claimed as novel in the repair.

value.rationale: The exact joint region is the finite-dimensional invariant controlling every affine adjacency filter and hence every polynomial filter on this quotient. The opposite-sign directions are needed for shifted adjacency and other non-Markov filters, for which idleness comparisons cannot give the amplification. The Petersen hexagon versus the stable parallelogram for n≥6 gives a genuine change in the optimization, including a flat branch for small positive shifts on Petersen. The positive heat calculations alone would be routine applications of prior theorems and were removed as a contribution.
